summary: In a workshop, Ray repairs and tests a robotic rat, replacing a faulty relay and new limbs, then performs maintenance while a diagnostic server exchanges data with the rat through a co-ax line. As he finishes, a large, imposing figure named Ziggy calls his name down a gangway, and Ray reluctantly prepares to turn around. The passage establishes Ziggy as a former hardware hacker now in administrative oversight, whom Ray is the only person to call Ziggy.
one_line: Ray finishes servicing a robotic rat in a workshop when the imposing Ziggy, a retired hardware hacker, calls him from down the gangway.
key_facts: Ray has attached new limbs to the robotic rat from his stockpile of spare parts.
The rat's crampon problem was caused by a bad electrical relay, which Ray replaced before attaching the new limbs.
A co-ax fiber line runs from the rat's anus to the diagnostic server array, plugged into an access port in the back.
Ray has examined the rat's carapace for structural integrity flaws and checked about three dozen servo-motors that serve as joints.
Ray has taken apart the supposedly hermetically sealed sensor boxes and run them through computer mediated test cycles.
Ray touches an electrode stylus to contact nodes and scans the single line LCD display for irregular messages.
Ray unscrews the co-ax cable and closes the motherboard access panel in the rat's flank when he finishes.
Ray is performing standard maintenance so he may not have to see the rat again for about a hundred thousand kilometers.
Ray has a personal policy that turning around is a bad idea.
Ziggy booms Ray's name down a cavernous gangway with a mix of menace and psychic exhaustion.
Ignoring Ziggy would constitute a career-ending bad idea for Ray.
Ziggy is a large black man, balding, with a devastating fu-manchu moustache.
Ziggy is a hardware hacker retired to administrative oversight.
Ray is the only one who calls him Ziggy; everyone else refers to him as Section.
